datasets.name: curated set of 33episodes described in Sec. 3.2

methods.name: ORCA
methods.description: Optimal Reciprocal Collision Avoidance, an efficient navigation planner that provides theoretical non-collision guarantees assuming all agents in the environment use the same planning policy

methods.name: SA-CADRL
methods.description: Socially aware collision avoidance with deep reinforcement learning, a social navigation method which formulates social navigation as a cooperative multi-agent collision avoidance problem with well-crafted rules to inject social awareness

methods.name: Social Forces
methods.description: A formulation to explain pedestrian navigation behavior as being under the influence of "social forces" including an attractive force to their goal, a repulsive force from other pedestrians and obstacles, and other attractive forces to interesting objects or other pedestrians in the environment.

methods.name: CADRL
methods.description: A recent, popular, and relatively state-of-the-art model using a deep reinforcement learning-based navigation method.

methods.name: pedestrian-unaware baseline
methods.description: A simple baseline algorithm evaluated on SocNavBench.

methods.name: meta planner
methods.description: Plans a sub-goal within a 6-second horizon (around 4–7 meters) each time a new checkpoint is requested without kinematic constraint application.

methods.name: 3D unicycle model
methods.description: A position and heading model used to account for kinematic constraints.

methods.name: meta-level planner
methods.description: A sampling planner that samples trajectories from a connectivity graph, evaluates them via heuristic cost functions, and returns the minimum cost trajectory within a budget to identify near-future waypoints and avoid obstacles.
